subject: chemistry-hl
topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
about: Original practice questions written for NevaIB from the IB guide's syllabus understandings and the school's unit order. Not IB past-paper questions, not publisher material and not IB markschemes: the marking points are written for self-marking. Organisms, experiments and data in data-response items are invented for practice.

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem: Elements in the same group of the periodic table have the same:
choices: Number of electron shells
Number of neutrons
Atomic mass
Number of valence electrons
items.note: Groups share outer electron configurations, so similar chemical properties. Periods share the number of occupied shells.

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem: Going down group 1, the reactivity of the metals:
choices: Increases, because the outer electron is lost more easily
Decreases, because the atoms get larger and hold their outer electron more tightly
Increases, because the nuclear charge decreases
Stays the same, because they have one valence electron
items.note: Larger atoms with more shielding hold the outer electron less strongly, so it is lost more easily.

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem: Which oxide dissolves in water to form an acidic solution?
choices: Na₂O
MgO
SO₃
CaO
items.note: Non-metal oxides are acidic (SO₃ → H₂SO₄). Metal oxides are basic (Na₂O → NaOH).

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem: Across period 3 from Na to Cl, atomic radius:
choices: Increases, because more electrons are added to each atom and they repel each other more strongly
Decreases, because nuclear charge increases while shielding stays similar
Decreases, because more shells are added
Stays the same, because electrons enter the same shell
items.note: Greater nuclear charge pulls the same shell closer.

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
choices: The ability of an atom to attract a bonding pair of electrons
The energy released when a gaseous atom gains an electron to form a negative ion
The energy needed to remove an electron from an atom
The charge on an ion of the element
items.note: Electronegativity increases across a period and up a group; fluorine is highest.

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem: When chlorine water is added to potassium bromide solution:
choices: No reaction occurs, because bromine is more reactive
Chlorine forms, because bromide is oxidised
Potassium chloride precipitates as a white solid
Bromine forms, because chlorine is more reactive than bromine
items.note: Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + Br₂ (orange/yellow). A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive one.

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem: Which ion is smaller than its atom?
choices: Cl⁻
O²⁻
Na⁺
S²⁻
items.note: Cations lose the outer shell and are smaller. Anions gain electrons, increasing repulsion, so they are larger.

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem: Which property is characteristic of transition elements?
choices: Low melting points
Variable oxidation states
Only colourless compounds
Single fixed ionic charge
items.note: Transition elements show variable oxidation states, coloured compounds, catalytic activity and complex ion formation.

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem: Transition elements show variable oxidation states because:
choices: They have very few electrons in total
The 4s and 3d sublevels are close in energy
Their 3d sublevel is always full
They have large atomic radii
items.note: Electrons from both 4s and 3d can be lost with similar energy, giving several possible ion charges.

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem: Zinc is in the d-block but is not considered a transition element because:
choices: Its atoms have no 3d electrons
It forms many coloured compounds
It has no 4s electrons in the atom
Its only ion, Zn²⁺, has a full 3d sublevel
items.note: A transition element forms at least one stable ion with a partially filled d sublevel. Zn²⁺ is [Ar] 3d¹⁰.

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem: What is the oxidation state of iron in [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻?

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem: Describe the reaction of sodium with water and write a balanced equation.
markscheme: Sodium floats, melts into a ball, fizzes/moves around (1)
Hydrogen gas and an alkaline solution form (1)
items.tactic: Describe = observations; include state symbols in the equation.

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem: Explain the trend in first ionisation energy down group 1.
markscheme: Ionisation energy decreases down the group (1)
Atomic radius increases / outer electron further from the nucleus (1)
More shielding by inner shells, so weaker attraction despite larger nuclear charge (1)
items.tactic: Trend first, then distance and shielding.

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem: Explain why transition element compounds are often coloured.
markscheme: Ligands split the d orbitals into two energy levels (1)
Electrons absorb light of a specific frequency to move to the higher level (1)
Requires a partially filled d sublevel (1)
items.tactic: Coloured compounds: splitting, absorption, complementary colour.

items.topicLabel: S3.1 The periodic table: classification of elements
items.stem:
Data response (data booklet values). Atomic (covalent) radii in pm for period 3: Na 160, Mg 140, Al 124, Si 114, P 109, S 104, Cl 100. First ionisation energies (kJ mol⁻¹): Na 496, Mg 738, Al 578, Si 787, P 1012, S 1000, Cl 1251.
(a) Describe the trend in atomic radius. (b) Identify the two exceptions to the increase in ionisation energy. (c) Explain one of the exceptions.
markscheme: (a) Radius decreases from Na (160 pm) to Cl (100 pm) (1)
(b) Mg to Al and P to S (1)
(c) Al: electron removed from 3p, higher energy/shielded by 3s; or S: paired 3p electron repelled, easier to remove (1)
Correct link to electron configuration given (1)
items.tactic: Data questions: quote values with units when describing a trend, then explain with nuclear charge, shielding and sublevels.
